text.p: Intermet Corp and Sudbury Inc said on Monday they had signed a definitive merger agreement under which Intermet will acquire all of the outstanding shares of Sudbury's common stock for $12.50 each in cash.
Sudbury has about 15.6 million shares outstanding on a fully diluted basis, with 4.2 million shares represented by stock options and participation certificates.

Under the agreement, a wholly owned subsidiary of Intermet will start a cash tender offer for Sudbury shares at $12.50 each. After the tender offer, the Intermet subsidiary will be merged into Sudbury, and holders of any remaining Sudbury common stock will receive the same consideration.
Completion of the acquisition is subject to the tender of 7.8 million Sudbury shares and the expiration or termination of any waiting periods under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act.
The combined company will have annual sales of about $845 million, the companies said.

Intermet is a ferrous casting foundry company with fiscal year 1995 sales of $542 million. The company designs, manufactures and machines precision iron and aluminium parts for automotive and industrial markets in North America and Europe.
Sudbury is a Tier 1 supplier of parts and services to original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) in the automotive industry.
